linked_issues.title: Mutating nested dict entries through dict.values() / dict.items() bypasses dirty tracking: rendered values and cached vars go stale

unresolved.first_comment: P2: These replacement views drop the native dict-view `.mapping` attribute, so `state.data.values().mapping` and `state.data.items().mapping` now raise `AttributeError`. Expose a proxy-backed read-only mapping so callers retain the dict-view API without bypassing nested mutation tracking.

**View `mapping` access breaks** The replacement views drop the native dict view’s `mapping` property, which is available on every supported Python version. Code such as `self.inventory.values().mapping["tea"]` now raises `AttributeError`. Add a read-only `mapping` property that reads through the owning proxy, and test it for both views.
